Fifteen comments

Strop the Razor

Nice simple tune with room for variation. I’ve also heard the last few bars played.
~B3 ~c3|~d3 d2e| ~=f3 fde| ~=fag ^fdc:|

I picked this up from a John Skelton Recording

↳ Posted by b.maloney on May 20th, 2002.

This tune appears on Ronan Browne and Peadar O‘Loughlin’s ’The South West Wind‘, but bearing the proabably incorrect title ’Petticoat Loose’ (which is another tune entirely).
They play the last phrase thus:

~B3 ~c3|~d3 d2e| ~=f3 fde| ~^fag fdc:|

i.e. F-natural in the penultimate bar, but with both Fs in the last bar played sharp.

↳ Posted by CreadurMawnOrganig on January 10th, 2004.

Liam O’Flynn calls it 3The Leg of the Duck"

On his first Album, Liam O’Flynn calls this jig “The Leg of the Duck”. He plays it after “Fraher’s Jig” and “I buried My Wife and Danced on Top of Her”

↳ Posted by Pierre Commes on April 27th, 2007.

You might like to ‘sharpen’ the C (hi hi) and ‘blunt’ (ha ha) the F’s in the last but 3 and last but 2 bars, respectively.

Strop The Razor, X:6

Another from the PW Joyce collection. This one is #94. A little different than the versions above it. In the notes Joyce says he collected it “From James Buckley, a Limerick piper”. The original key in the collection is B-flat (which would likely mean James had a set pitched around B-flat), but it fits nicely in D on the modern pipes, with no keys, or in G if you’ve a F key (or you’re particularly good half-holing it).

↳ Posted by daveboling on February 2nd, 2017.

Strop The Razor, X:7

Setting in G Major with three F Naturals. Interesting to see that the settings of this tune can be so different. This one is very similar to setting number 6. The only difference that I consider important is that there are three F Naturals instead of one.

Not sure where I got this setting. It could be from the concertina lessons given by Noel Hill in the Irish Club in Galway city, I remember this was one of the tunes he taught the children and me (I was the only adult in the class, and the only one with an English system concertina). Maybe I just got it from the sessions in Galway city, although this is not an standard session tune.

↳ Posted by Fernando Durbán Galnares on October 11th, 2020.

Re: Strop The Razor

Strop the Razor and Petticoat Loose are distinct tunes: https://tunearch.org/wiki/Strop_the_Razor_(2) and https://tunearch.org/wiki/Petticoat_Loose_(2) I’m amazed no one else has picked up on this, they seem like cheese and chalk to my ear, not even a passing resemblance. Petticoat Loose is Leg of the Duck-ish.

Willie Clancy used the Strop title for X:3 or X:9 on Seoda Ceoil #1. On a tape made by Martin Talty he gives the title after playing it. Sean Keane called it by this name, he learned it from Willie. I think the mixup began with John Kelly And James Kelly’s 1974 record Irish Traditional Fiddle Music, where this title was applied to the other settings shown here. Note that Ronan Browne and Peadar O’Loughlin use the Petticoat title for those, Peadar was Willie’s friend.

Willie played a beautiful run of sixteenth notes in the 2nd part of Strop the Razor, which is very much like #1093 in O’Neill’s Music of Ireland, harkening back to the sruth mor (great stream) of the old harpists.

↳ Posted by What's the name of this tune? on December 29th, 2023.
